affiliations.date_precision: The 1938 annual report identifies his unit while listing a September-December 1938 service-school course; assignment start and end dates are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: A 1938 New York military report names Sergeant Louis Dups in the 101st Cavalry. An original OSS memorandum of 3 May 1945 names Major Louis Dups in the Cavalry, matching the indexed Major Louis Dups. This establishes an earlier military pathway, not the immediate predecessor or a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: In 1938, Louis Dups was a sergeant in Headquarters Troop, 101st Cavalry, New York National Guard. This is an earlier military assignment, not a documented immediate pre-OSS posting.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Sergeant Louis Dups, Headquarters Troop, 101st Cavalry.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1938 New York Adjutant General report places Sergeant Louis Dups in Headquarters Troop, 101st Cavalry, during a non-commissioned officers' course. A May 1945 OSS memorandum identifies a Major Louis Dups in the Cavalry, independently connecting the uncommon name and branch to OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: uncommon full name, the indexed Major rank, and the original 1945 OSS memorandum's Major Louis Dups and Cavalry branch corroborate the earlier named New York cavalry sergeant. Box 206 remains unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented in a 1938 report, before OSS existed. The sources do not establish when Dups entered OSS or which posting immediately preceded it.
claims.match_notes: The 1945 document is an identity and branch bridge only. No civilian employer is established, and no service number is public.

person_updates.identity_evidence: NARA page 128 row 31 prints Louis Dups, Maj, Box 206. The original 3 May 1945 OSS memorandum names Maj Louis Dups, Cav, and the 1938 New York report names Sergeant Louis Dups, Headquarters Troop, 101st Cavalry. Uncommon full name and Cavalry pathway support a high-confidence cross-record identity; the Box 206 personnel file has not been reviewed.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 206 for OSS entry date, immediate predecessor, and last civilian employer; do not infer either from the 1938 regiment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: NARA page 128 row 21 prints Capt Stephen W Dunwell, Box 206, without a protected identifier. IEEE and IBM document an engineer Stephen W. Dunwell who worked for IBM and served in the Army Security Agency, but neither source links him to the Box 206 OSS record. Name plus broadly compatible wartime rank is insufficient for this employer attribution.
person_updates.next_action: Inspect Box 206 or a direct OSS document linking the indexed Captain to the IBM engineer before assigning IBM as a last civilian employer; determine wartime chronology separately.
